summary: Lake of the Woods County, MN: an 80-foot tower moved from Warroad to the Northwest Angle in 1951 and later removed; no removal date or current site description found.

facts.design: 80-foot ladder tower; Warroad survey notes describe all-steel construction with a hexagon-shaped enclosed cab
facts.status_note: Removed. The county compilation says it was the northernmost lookout tower in the lower 48 states until removed; no removal date found.
facts.agency: Minnesota Forest Service (Mn MFS), state-owned; operated by Minnesota & Ontario Paper Co. (Mando) to protect its timber

events.note: Survey notes describe the Warroad state fire tower (Roseau County)

corrections.why: 166N-35W-2 is a township-range-section style land location, not an agency. The county compilation lists the owner as Mn MFS.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Roseau County survey notes call the Warroad tower 80 feet and also say about 100 feet high; the Lake of the Woods compilation and the 1950s article give 80 feet for the tower at the Angle. The record keeps 80 feet (24.4 m) and the story flags the disagreement.

The 1950s article says the State of Minnesota Department of Conservation owned the tower; the county compilations say Minnesota Forest Service (Mn MFS). Both name a state owner; the record uses Mn MFS.

sources.title: Lake of the Woods County Fire Lookout Towers

notes_for_editor: Brief's agency value (166N-35W-2) is a land location code and was corrected. Height is disputed inside the Roseau entry (80 vs about 100 ft). The tower moved from Warroad (Roseau County) in 1951. No removal year, access status or description of the site today was found in the sources read (two searches, four page reads). Staffing comes from a 1950s article reprinted on the Central Lookouts page. No new photos.
